hook_text: 84 sweets, 120 stickers. How many identical bags? Prime bricks answer in seconds.
clip_script: For larger numbers, factorisation is quicker. Write both factorisations side by side and take only the primes they SHARE. 84 is two, two, three, seven. 120 is two, two, two, three, five. Both have two twos — 84 only has two of them, so take two twos. Both have one three: take it. Seven is only in 84 and five is only in 120, so neither is shared. HCF equals two times two times three: 12.
visual_style: Two towers of coloured prime bricks for 84 and 120; shared bricks slide together into a 12 block that becomes 12 gift bags; then every brick stacks into an 840 bus timetable.
pacing: Quick ladders, slow comparison, snap to 12 and 840.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn when a problem wants the gift bags and when it wants the buses.
